standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the bound d and is what makes the projective dimension of H^n(K') drop by one.

core_obligations: Note that an object of D(R) is perfect exactly when it is bounded with finite cohomology modules, that strong generation is the notion of the derived-category definition, and write d = dim(R) (proof lines 20827-20832).
Reduce the claim to showing K lies in the (d + 1)-fold generated subcategory, using that every finite R-module has projective dimension at most d (proof lines 20835-20837).
State the induction hypothesis to be proved: for 0 <= i <= d, if H^n(K) has projective dimension at most i for all n, then K lies in the (i + 1)-fold generated subcategory (proof lines 20838-20840).

Base case i = 0: all cohomology modules are projective, hence Ext^r_R(H^n(K), H^m(K)) = 0 for r > 0, so K is isomorphic to the direct sum of the shifts of its cohomology modules, and since each is a finite projective module it is a summand of a sum of copies of R, giving K in the one-fold generated subcategory (proof lines 20843-20852).

Induction step, first part: for K with each H^n(K) of projective dimension at most i + 1, choose bounds a <= b outside which the cohomology vanishes and surjections F^n -> H^n(K) with F^n finite free, lift them to maps F^n[-n] -> K, and assemble the morphism bigoplus_{a <= n <= b} F^n[-n] -> K that is surjective on cohomology (proof lines 20855-20864).

Induction step, second part: complete it to the distinguished triangle K' -> bigoplus F^n[-n] -> K -> K'[1], observe that K' is bounded with finite cohomology, and read off the short exact sequences 0 -> H^n(K') -> F^n -> H^n(K) -> 0 (proof lines 20865-20874).

Conclude via the subadditivity of projective dimension that H^n(K') has projective dimension at most max(0, i), so K' lies in the (i + 1)-fold generated subcategory and therefore K lies in the (i + 2)-fold one, which is the desired induction step (proof lines 20875-20879).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a Noetherian regular ring R of finite dimension d is a strong generator for the full subcategory of perfect objects of D(R) (source lines 20819-20824). The proof is a genuine induction on the projective dimension bound, using the characterisation of perfect objects as bounded complexes with finite cohomology and the definition of generation in a bounded number of steps. It first records that every finite R-module has projective dimension at most d, so that d + 1 is the generation bound, then proves by induction on i that if every H^n(K) has projective dimension at most i then K lies in the i + 1-fold generated subcategory of R (proof lines 20832-20840). The base case i = 0 uses that projective cohomology modules have vanishing higher Ext between them, so that K splits as the direct sum of the shifts of its cohomology, and each finite projective module is a summand of a sum of copies of R (proof lines 20843-20852). The induction step is the substantive part: it picks a surjection from a finite free module onto each cohomology module, lifts these to maps F^n[-n] -> K in the derived category, takes the associated distinguished triangle K' -> bigoplus F^n[-n] -> K -> K'[1], reads off the short exact sequences 0 -> H^n(K') -> F^n -> H^n(K) -> 0, and uses the projective-dimension subadditivity to bound the projective dimension of H^n(K') by max(0, i), so that K' lies in the i+1-fold generated subcategory and hence K lies in the i+2-fold one (proof lines 20855-20879). The non-routine content is the bookkeeping of the generation index through the distinguished triangle, together with the projective-dimension drop that makes the induction go through.
